title: Leviticus Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 2.

questions.question: What kind of flour is to be used when offering a meat offering unto the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Fine flour
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:1 states the offering shall be of fine flour.

questions.question: What must be poured upon the meat offering along with fine flour?
questions.correctAnswer: Oil
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:1 instructs that oil shall be poured upon the offering.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 2, what is placed on the meat offering along with oil?
questions.correctAnswer: Frankincense
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:1 specifies that frankincense shall be put on the offering.

questions.question: Who is to receive the meat offering to perform the ritual?
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron's sons the priests
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:2 states the offering is brought to Aaron's sons the priests.

questions.question: What does the priest take from the meat offering to burn upon the altar?
options: A handful of flour, oil, and frankincense
questions.correctAnswer: A handful of flour, oil, and frankincense
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:2 explains the priest takes a handful of flour, oil, and frankincense to burn.

questions.question: What happens to the remainder of the meat offering after the priest burns the memorial?
options: It is given to the Levites
It is Aaron's and his sons'
It is eaten by the offerer
questions.correctAnswer: It is Aaron's and his sons'
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:3 states the remnant of the meat offering is Aaron's and his sons'.

questions.question: If the meat offering is baked in the oven, what type of cakes are to be made?
options: Unleavened cakes of fine flour mingled with oil
questions.correctAnswer: Unleavened cakes of fine flour mingled with oil
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:4 describes the meat offering baked in the oven as unleavened cakes mingled with oil.

questions.question: How is the meat offering prepared if it is baked in a pan?
options: Unleavened fine flour mingled with oil
questions.correctAnswer: Unleavened fine flour mingled with oil
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:5 indicates the pan-baked meat offering is unleavened fine flour mingled with oil.

questions.question: What must be done to the meat offering after baking in a pan before it is presented?
options: Part it in pieces and pour oil on it
questions.correctAnswer: Part it in pieces and pour oil on it
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:6 commands to part it in pieces and pour oil upon it as the meat offering.

questions.question: True or False: The meat offering must always contain leaven according to Leviticus 2.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:11 states no meat offering shall be made with leaven.

questions.question: True or False: The priest burns a memorial of the meat offering on the altar as an offering by fire, a sweet savour unto the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:2 and 2:9 affirm the priest burns a memorial of the offering as a sweet savour to the LORD.

questions.question: Which seasoning must be added to every meat offering according to Leviticus 2?
questions.correctAnswer: Salt
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:13 requires every meat offering to be seasoned with salt.

questions.question: True or False: Honey is allowed to be burned in any offering made by fire in Leviticus 2.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:11 forbids burning honey in offerings made by fire.

questions.question: What comes first in the instructions in Leviticus 2:1-6?
options: Pour oil on the meat offering
Bring the offering to Aaron's sons
Bake the meat offering in a pan
Put frankincense on the meat offering
questions.correctAnswer: Pour oil on the meat offering
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:1 commands the offering shall have oil poured on it before other steps are described.

questions.question: True or False: The meat offering's remnant is considered most holy and belongs to Aaron and his sons.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:3 and 2:10 state the remainder is most holy and belongs to Aaron and his sons.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 2:7, what ingredients must a meat offering baked in the fryingpan contain?
questions.correctAnswer: Fine flour with oil
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:7 clearly states that a meat offering baked in the fryingpan shall be made of fine flour with oil.

questions.question: What is the role of the priest when a meat offering is presented, as described in Leviticus 2:8?
options: To bring the meat offering to the altar
To eat the entire meat offering
To sprinkle the offering with water
To offer a prayer for the offerer
questions.correctAnswer: To bring the meat offering to the altar
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:8 instructs that when the meat offering is presented to the priest, he shall bring it to the altar.

questions.question: What does the priest do with a memorial portion of the meat offering according to Leviticus 2:9?
options: Burns it upon the altar as an offering made by fire
Eats it with the other priests
questions.correctAnswer: Burns it upon the altar as an offering made by fire
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:9 explains that the priest shall take a memorial from the meat offering and burn it upon the altar as an offering made by fire, which is a sweet savour to the LORD.

questions.question: What happens to the remnant of the meat offering after the priest burns the memorial portion, as explained in Leviticus 2:10?
options: It becomes the possession of Aaron and his sons
It is discarded outside the camp
It is given back to the offerer
It is burned completely on the altar
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes the possession of Aaron and his sons
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:10 states that what remains of the meat offering after the memorial portion is burned belongs to Aaron and his sons and is considered most holy.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 2:11, which two substances are forbidden in any meat offering made by fire?
questions.correctAnswer: Leaven and honey
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:11 forbids the use of leaven and honey in any meat offering made by fire, emphasizing purity and obedience.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 2:12, the oblation of the firstfruits is burnt on the altar for a sweet savour.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:12 clearly states that the oblation of the firstfruits is offered to the LORD but shall not be burnt on the altar for a sweet savour.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 2:13 teach about the importance of the covenant in offerings?
options: Every meat offering must be seasoned with salt, symbolizing the salt of the covenant
Offerings must be leavened to show growth
Honey must be added to every meat offering
The priest must sprinkle water on the offering
questions.correctAnswer: Every meat offering must be seasoned with salt, symbolizing the salt of the covenant
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:13 instructs that every meat offering must be seasoned with salt, which represents the salt of the covenant of God, highlighting the seriousness and integrity of the offering.

questions.question: What is the significance of the green ears of corn dried by fire in the firstfruits offering described in Leviticus 2:14?
options: They represent the offering of firstfruits for the meat offering
They are used to make leavened bread
They are consumed by the priests directly
They symbolize sin in the offering
questions.correctAnswer: They represent the offering of firstfruits for the meat offering
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:14 describes that green ears of corn dried by fire, beaten out of full ears, are offered as the meat offering of the firstfruits, symbolizing dedication and thanksgiving to God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 2:15, oil and frankincense must be placed on the firstfruits meat offering.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:15 instructs that oil is put upon the offering and frankincense laid thereon, making it a proper meat offering.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 2:16 say the priest shall burn as a memorial of the firstfruits meat offering?
options: Part of the beaten corn, part of the oil, and all the frankincense
questions.correctAnswer: Part of the beaten corn, part of the oil, and all the frankincense
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:16 states that the priest shall burn a memorial portion consisting of part of the beaten corn, part of the oil, and all the frankincense as an offering made by fire unto the LORD.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 2:9 promise will happen if the priest burns a memorial portion of the meat offering on the altar as instructed in Leviticus 2:8?
options: It becomes an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD
The people must fast for a day
The offering is returned to the offerer
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:9 explains that when the priest burns the memorial portion on the altar as instructed in Leviticus 2:8, it becomes an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour to the LORD, symbolizing acceptance and worship.

questions.question: Based on Leviticus 2:11 and 2:12, how does this passage teach about obedience and reverence in offerings?
options: Offerings must exclude leaven and honey and firstfruits must not be burnt for a sweet savour
Leaven and honey are encouraged to enhance offerings
Firstfruits should always be burnt for a sweet savour
Offerings can include any ingredient as long as they are sincere
questions.correctAnswer: Offerings must exclude leaven and honey and firstfruits must not be burnt for a sweet savour
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:11 forbids leaven and honey in offerings, emphasizing purity, while 2:12 states firstfruits are offered but not burnt on the altar for a sweet savour, highlighting reverence and obedience.

questions.question: A believer struggles with knowing how to honor God with their offerings. What biblical truth from Leviticus 2:13 teaches about integrity in offerings?
options: Every offering must be seasoned with salt, symbolizing the covenant which must not be lacking
Offerings are acceptable only if they contain honey
The amount of offering determines God's acceptance
Offerings can be made with leaven if sincerity is present
questions.correctAnswer: Every offering must be seasoned with salt, symbolizing the covenant which must not be lacking
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:13 teaches that salt, representing the covenant of God, must not be lacking in any offering, symbolizing faithfulness and integrity in worship.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 2:10 teaches that what remains of the meat offering is common and not considered holy.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:10 states that the remainder of the meat offering is most holy and belongs to Aaron and his sons, indicating it is sacred and set apart.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 2:8 imply about the role of the believer when bringing a meat offering?
options: The believer must bring the properly prepared offering to the LORD through the priest
The believer should burn the offering themselves
The believer may eat the offering before presenting it
The offering can be leavened if desired
questions.correctAnswer: The believer must bring the properly prepared offering to the LORD through the priest
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:8 directs that the meat offering made of specified ingredients must be brought unto the LORD and presented to the priest, emphasizing the believer's role in obedience and proper worship.

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 2:13, what ingredient must never be lacking in any meat offering as part of the covenant?
questions.correctAnswer: Salt
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:13 commands that every oblation of the meat offering must be seasoned with salt, symbolizing the 'salt of the covenant' of God which must not be lacking.

questions.question: Leviticus 2:14 instructs that the meat offering of firstfruits should consist of what?
options: Green ears of corn dried by fire
questions.correctAnswer: Green ears of corn dried by fire
questions.explanation: The verse specifies that for the meat offering of firstfruits, green ears of corn dried by fire, beaten out of full ears, are to be offered.

questions.question: What two substances are to be put upon the firstfruits offering of corn as described in Leviticus 2:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Oil and frankincense
questions.explanation: Verse 15 commands that oil shall be put upon the offering and frankincense laid thereon, marking it as a meat offering.

questions.question: In Leviticus 2:16, what part of the firstfruits offering is burned by the priest as a memorial?
options: Part of the beaten corn, part of the oil, and all the frankincense
All of the beaten corn and oil
questions.correctAnswer: Part of the beaten corn, part of the oil, and all the frankincense
questions.explanation: The priest burns a memorial portion consisting of part of the beaten corn, part of the oil, and all of the frankincense as an offering made by fire to the LORD.

questions.question: What does the use of salt in all offerings as mentioned in Leviticus 2:13 symbolize in the ancient Israelite covenant context?
options: Purity and preservation of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Purity and preservation of the covenant
questions.explanation: Salt in the ancient Near East symbolized purity and preservation, reflecting the enduring nature of God's covenant as referenced in Leviticus 2:13.

questions.question: Leviticus 2 forbids the use of which two ingredients in any meat offering made by fire, according to verse 11?
questions.correctAnswer: Leaven and honey
questions.explanation: Verse 11 explicitly forbids leaven and honey in any meat offering made by fire because these were not to be burned on the altar as a sweet savour to the LORD.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also emphasizes the importance of salt in covenant and offerings, connecting to Leviticus 2:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 18:19
questions.explanation: Numbers 18:19 mentions the 'salt of the covenant' in relation to offerings, echoing Leviticus 2:13's emphasis on salt in covenant offerings.

questions.question: What cross-biblical theme is echoed by Leviticus 2:1-2 regarding offerings made by fire of a sweet savour to the LORD?
options: The typology of Christ as a perfect offering in Hebrews 13:10-16
questions.correctAnswer: The typology of Christ as a perfect offering in Hebrews 13:10-16
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:10-16 describes Jesus as the perfect offering, fulfilling the sacrificial system of Leviticus 2:1-2's offerings made by fire of a sweet savour to God.

questions.question: Which literary device is exhibited in Leviticus 2:13-16 by the repetition and inclusion of salt, oil, and frankincense in the offerings?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The repeated mention of salt, oil, and frankincense at the start and end of the passage (verses 13 and 16) forms an inclusio framing the section on meat offerings.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'meat offering' (minchah) in Leviticus 2, and how does it inform the understanding of these offerings?
options: A gift or tribute; emphasizing voluntary worship
questions.correctAnswer: A gift or tribute; emphasizing voluntary worship
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'minchah' means 'gift' or 'tribute,' highlighting that meat offerings were voluntary gifts of worship and thanksgiving presented to God, as in Leviticus 2.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 2:12, the oblation of the firstfruits is burnt entirely on the altar for a sweet savour.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:12 states that the oblation of the firstfruits shall be offered unto the LORD but shall not be burnt on the altar for a sweet savour.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 2:10 declares that the remnant of the meat offering belongs to Aaron and his sons and is considered most holy.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:10 specifies that what is left of the meat offering belongs to Aaron and his sons and is regarded as most holy of the offerings of the LORD made by fire.

questions.question: How does the requirement to offer salt with all offerings in Leviticus 2:13 foreshadow the New Testament concept in Mark 9:50?
options: Salt as a symbol of purity and covenant loyalty
Salt as a metaphor for judgement
questions.correctAnswer: Salt as a symbol of purity and covenant loyalty
questions.explanation: Mark 9:50 references being 'at peace with one another, salted with salt,' symbolizing purity and covenant loyalty, paralleling Leviticus 2:13's salt of the covenant.

questions.question: Leviticus 2:14-16 describe a specific preparation of the firstfruits offering involving corn dried by fire and oil. How does this preparation connect with ancient Near Eastern agricultural practices?
options: Drying grain by fire preserved it and symbolized offering the fruits of labor to God
The corn was fermented for alcoholic offerings
The corn was mixed with meat for a mixed offering
Green ears were only used for secular feasts
questions.correctAnswer: Drying grain by fire preserved it and symbolized offering the fruits of labor to God
questions.explanation: Drying grain by fire was a common preservation method in the ancient Near East, and offering such prepared grain symbolized giving the best and preserved fruits of one’s labor to God, as in Leviticus 2:14-16.

questions.question: Which New Testament book parallels the concept of offerings made by fire of a sweet savour to the LORD as described in Leviticus 2:9 and 16?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation
questions.explanation: Revelation 8 describes incense and prayers of the saints as a sweet savour offering before God, paralleling the burnt memorial offerings in Leviticus 2:9 and 16.

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 2:1, what must accompany the fine flour in a meat offering to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Oil and frankincense
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:1 states that the meat offering must be of fine flour with oil poured upon it and frankincense put thereon as part of the offering.

questions.question: What does the priest do with the memorial portion of the meat offering as described in Leviticus 2:2?
options: Burns it upon the altar as a sweet savour to the LORD
Eats it in the holy place
Saves it for the next offering
questions.correctAnswer: Burns it upon the altar as a sweet savour to the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:2 explains that the priest takes a handful of flour, oil, and frankincense and burns it on the altar as a memorial, producing a sweet savour to the LORD.

questions.question: What is the status of the remainder of the meat offering after the memorial is burned, according to Leviticus 2:3?
options: It belongs to Aaron and his sons and is considered most holy
It must be destroyed outside the camp
It is given to the Levites for their service
It is eaten by the offerer
questions.correctAnswer: It belongs to Aaron and his sons and is considered most holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:3 states the remnant of the meat offering is given to Aaron and his sons and is regarded as a most holy thing of the LORD's fire offerings.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the type of leaven allowed in meat offerings according to Leviticus 2:11?
options: No leaven is allowed in any meat offering
Only a small amount of leaven is allowed
Leaven is allowed if mixed with oil
questions.correctAnswer: No leaven is allowed in any meat offering
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:11 explicitly forbids any meat offering to be made with leaven, stating that no leaven or honey shall be burned in offerings made by fire to the LORD.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 2:13 teach about seasoning meat offerings?
options: Every meat offering must be seasoned with salt, symbolizing the covenant of God
Meat offerings should be sweetened with honey
Salt is optional in meat offerings
Only offerings of animals require salt
questions.correctAnswer: Every meat offering must be seasoned with salt, symbolizing the covenant of God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:13 commands that every meat offering be seasoned with salt, which is called the salt of the covenant of God, emphasizing the covenantal nature of offerings.

questions.question: How do verses 4 and 7 together inform us about the preparation methods of meat offerings?
options: Meat offerings can be baked in an oven, pan, or frying pan but must be unleavened and mixed with oil
Meat offerings must be boiled and leavened
Only raw grain can be offered in meat offerings
Meat offerings require fermentation before baking
questions.correctAnswer: Meat offerings can be baked in an oven, pan, or frying pan but must be unleavened and mixed with oil
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:4 describes meat offerings baked in the oven as unleavened cakes or wafers with oil, while verse 7 includes frying pan preparations with fine flour and oil, highlighting preparation variety but strict unleavened and oily mixture requirements.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Leviticus 2:12 and 2:14 provide about firstfruits offerings?
options: Firstfruits are offered to the LORD but are not burnt on the altar as a sweet savour
Firstfruits must always be burnt completely on the altar
Firstfruits offerings can include leaven and honey
questions.correctAnswer: Firstfruits are offered to the LORD but are not burnt on the altar as a sweet savour
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:12 says firstfruits are offered but not burnt for a sweet savour, while 2:14 specifies offering green ears of corn dried by fire, indicating a distinct treatment and symbolism for firstfruits separate from other meat offerings.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 2:16 deepen our understanding of the priest’s role in the offering process?
options: The priest burns a memorial part of the beaten corn, oil, and frankincense as an offering by fire to the LORD
The priest consumes the entire offering himself
The priest returns the offering to the offerer without any burning
The priest only offers the oil and discards the rest
questions.correctAnswer: The priest burns a memorial part of the beaten corn, oil, and frankincense as an offering by fire to the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:16 specifies the priest’s duty to burn a memorial portion of the meal offering—beaten corn, oil, and frankincense—demonstrating the priest’s mediatorial role in presenting offerings to God.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the command in Leviticus 2:9 that the offering burned upon the altar is a 'sweet savour' unto the LORD?
options: God’s holiness and delight in obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and delight in obedience
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:9 shows that God values the obedience and proper worship symbolized by the sweet savour of the burnt offering, reflecting His holiness and delight in covenant faithfulness (cf. Psalm 51:16-17).

questions.question: What theological principle is taught by the repeated statement in Leviticus 2:3 and 2:10 that the leftover meat offering is 'most holy' and belongs to Aaron and his sons?
options: The sanctification of the priesthood and their dependence on God’s provision
The offering is to be eaten by the people
The priests must destroy the leftovers
The leftovers belong to the temple treasury
questions.correctAnswer: The sanctification of the priesthood and their dependence on God’s provision
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize that the leftover meat offerings are most holy and belong to the priests, teaching the doctrine that the priesthood is set apart and sustained by God through His offerings (Leviticus 2:3, 2:10).

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth about covenant faithfulness is illustrated by the requirement of salt in every offering as stated in Leviticus 2:13?
options: The salt symbolizes the enduring nature of God's covenant with His people
Salt is a preservative for physical offerings only
Salt is optional and symbolic of human effort
questions.correctAnswer: The salt symbolizes the enduring nature of God's covenant with His people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:13 teaches that salt, called the salt of the covenant, must not be lacking, symbolizing the permanence and faithfulness of God's covenant relationship with Israel.

questions.question: What sceptical objection might be raised against the detailed regulations on meat offerings in Leviticus 2:1–16, and how does this chapter respond to that objection?
options: Sceptics claim the offerings are mere ritual with no spiritual value; Leviticus 2 teaches these offerings symbolize holiness, covenant, and God's delight in obedience
Sceptics claim the offerings are too complicated to understand; Leviticus 2 clarifies instructions to simplify worship
Sceptics claim offerings were optional; Leviticus 2 shows they were merely cultural traditions
Sceptics claim offerings were only for the priests; Leviticus 2 confirms only priests participated
questions.correctAnswer: Sceptics claim the offerings are mere ritual with no spiritual value; Leviticus 2 teaches these offerings symbolize holiness, covenant, and God's delight in obedience
questions.explanation: Sceptics may dismiss these offerings as empty ritual, but Leviticus 2 reveals their deep theological significance—symbolizing sanctification, covenant faithfulness, and God’s pleasure in obedient worship (Leviticus 2:1-3, 2:13, 2:9).

questions.question: How do Leviticus 2:8 and 2:9 together illustrate the priest’s mediatorial role in the Old Testament sacrificial system?
options: The priest receives the meat offering and burns a memorial portion on the altar, acting as intermediary between people and God
The priest consumes all offerings without involvement with the altar
The priest prepares the offering but has no role in burning it
The priest gives the offering back to the worshiper
questions.correctAnswer: The priest receives the meat offering and burns a memorial portion on the altar, acting as intermediary between people and God
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:8 shows the priest receiving the offering and 2:9 describes burning a memorial portion on the altar, highlighting the priest’s essential role as mediator presenting the people’s offerings to God.

questions.question: What Christological foreshadowing can be drawn from the continual theme of offerings being burned as a 'sweet savour' in Leviticus 2:1–9?
options: Christ’s perfect sacrifice is the ultimate sweet savour pleasing to God
Christ was the priest who burned the offerings
Christ’s ministry involved offering grain and oil sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s perfect sacrifice is the ultimate sweet savour pleasing to God
questions.explanation: The repeated mention of offerings as a sweet savour foreshadows Christ’s once-for-all sacrifice, which perfectly satisfies God’s justice and pleases Him (cf. Ephesians 5:2; Hebrews 9:14).

questions.question: What do Leviticus 2:5-6 together teach about the nature of the meat offering in terms of sanctification?
options: The offering must be unleavened, mixed with oil, and divided before oil is poured on it, symbolizing purification and dedication
The offering can contain leaven if mixed with oil
The offering is to be eaten raw by the priests
The offering is only a symbol with no ritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: The offering must be unleavened, mixed with oil, and divided before oil is poured on it, symbolizing purification and dedication
questions.explanation: Leviticus 2:5-6 describe the meat offering as unleavened flour mixed with oil, parted in pieces, and anointed with oil, pointing to the sanctifying and dedicatory nature of the offering.
